rationale: Surfaced by the 024 US3 stale-config re-entry case (hrt-up-image-single-feature-stale-config). Re-entering a workspace whose configuration has CHANGED since its container was created: the reference reattaches to the existing container, deacon provisions a new one. Measured directly at oracle 0.87.0 against fx-up-stale-config — two `up` runs whose documents differ only in `name` and `containerEnv.CONF_GENERATION` return the IDENTICAL containerId from `devcontainer up` and two different containerIds from `deacon up`. deacon is the stricter side and deliberately so: its container identity includes a configHash (ext-container-identity-labels, a label the reference does not set), so a changed document is a different identity. Reattaching is the dangerous branch — the container keeps the Feature layer built from the OLD configuration while every reported value comes from the NEW one — which is the failure the recreate avoids. SPEC POSITION, stated against the strongest text rather than around it: devcontainer-reference.md §Environment Resume covers resuming from a STOPPED state and says nothing about a configuration that has changed, so there is no re-entry policy to follow. The nearest passage cuts the other way and is cited here so the record does not read as if it did not exist — feature-dependencies.md §Image Metadata: 'For subsequent creations from an image (or resumes of a dev container), the dependency tree is not re-calculated. To re-calculate the dependency tree, the user must delete the image (or dev container) and recreate it from a devcontainer.json.' That describes resumption REUSING, and puts the recreate burden on the user, which is nearer the reference's reattach than to deacon's automatic recreate. It is descriptive of dependency-tree recalculation rather than a MUST about re-entry, so it does not make deacon nonconformant and the spec axis stays `unspecified`; but it is the strongest spec text bearing on this choice, and a reader weighing the waiver deserves to see it. The argument for recreating is a safety one, not a spec one: the passage assumes the configuration is unchanged, and says nothing about the case where it is not — which is precisely where reattaching serves a container built from a document that no longer exists. Separately tracked and NOT waived: deacon leaves the superseded container RUNNING, so one workspace ends up with two live containers (https://github.com/get2knowio/deacon/issues/371). The recreate is the decision; the leak is a bug. This waiver self-invalidates as stale when the difference stops reproducing.
